Dialysis tubing can act as a partially permeable membrane because it has microscopic holes
that allow small soluble molecules to pass through by diffusion.
You are going to investigate the molecules that can diffuse through dialysis tubing.
Read all the instructions but DO NOT CARRY THEM OUT until you have drawn a table
for your results in the space provided in 1(a)(i).
You should use the safety equipment provided while you are carrying out the practical work.
Step 1 Remove the piece of dialysis tubing from the beaker of water labelled W. It has been
knotted at one end to form a bag. Gently rub the unknotted end of the dialysis tubing
until it is open.
Step 2 Use a syringe to put 10 cm of solution M into the open end of the dialysis tubing bag.
Step 3 Hold the open end of the bag and rinse the outside of the dialysis tubing by dipping it
into the water in beaker W.

Starch can be broken down into reducing sugars. The enzyme amylase catalyses this
reaction.
Plan an investigation to find out the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme amylase.
